newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: All eyes on Asia as Allianz news unfolds.
newsitem.headline: All eyes on Asia as Allianz news unfolds.

text.p: All eyes in the insurance world turned again to Asia last week on news that giant German insurance group Allianz AG Holding planned to strengthen its ties with Australian general insurer MMI Insurance.

A statement issued by MMI said it planned to take a 20 percent stake in Allianz (Singapore) Pte Ltd for A$23.9 million and that in return Allianz would buy an additional 20 percent of MMI stock at A$4.00 per share, raising its total holding to 38 percent.
News of the deal hit the headlines a day after a report that said Allianz had secured an underwriting licence for Shanghai, China.

But, while the stories made good copy, neither has had a beneficial effect on relations with regulators in the region, said Michael Diekmann, the Singapore-based chief executive officer for Asia-Pacific of Allianz AG Holding.
"Asia is a sensitive market to be trading in and premature stories can have a damaging effect on negotiations," he said in an interview with Reuters on Thursday.

Diekmann, who heads the Allianz unit implementing group strategy in Asia, said he was surprised to see news of the widely-predicted Chinese licence being published as fact before it was confirmed by the Chinese authorities.
News reports had placed the source of the story as European Commission vice-president Sir Leon Brittan who had been heading a trade mission to Beijing.
"Making predictions is not always helpful," said Diekmann. "The news on both counts was probably a little premature."
Not surprisingly, his comments on the MMI proposals are guarded. "We can't comment on specifics of the deal until it is completed and the shareholders have voted," he said.
Allianz Singapore is the group's principal underwriting unit in Asia, although with about Singapore $250 million in premiums annually, it only contributes about 0.4 percent of group totals.
This total is planned to grow to a full one percent by 2000 and will be fuelled "by as much organic growth as possible," Diekmann said.
Expected premium growth from a closer relationship with MMI would help both companies achieve long term goals, he added.

"To combine forces has certain advantages. In these markets you need a lot of human resources and financial strength to be successful, so joining forces and realising synergies is a motivating factor.
"We can say that we have a very sure indication that the tie-up with MMI would increase the business perspectives in the region for both companies substantially," he said.
Even with a lack of specific detail, the moves in themselves serve to underline the importance with which Allianz views its Asian operations and their role in the group's future.
Allianz already has underwriting companies in Asia -- in Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore and two in Indonesia (one life and one general) -- plus an asset management unit, also in Hong Kong.
Additionally, it has a 10 percent stake in a Thai insurer and representative offices in India, Vietnam and three in China.
